title: ADR-00 Topology, tick barrier and determinism
outcome: Process topology (gateway, witness, one subprocess per agent, signer handles, sockets) and the gateway-as-scheduler tick barrier that makes seeded runs reproducible; due 24 Nov
acceptance: ADR file ≤900 words with sections Context, Decision, Consequences, Interface touched (which of C1–C6), Tests that prove it
Decision specifies the tick barrier: one envelope or no-op per agent per tick, executed in agent_id order, gateway assigns seq/ts/record_id
Names the determinism tests: same seed twice → byte-identical records; faulty run == S* before t0
States the key-isolation claim verbatim: enforced in production (uid/container), detected here by reconciliation
summary: ADR-00 written (899 words). Gateway (uid 0) spawns witness (uid 60000) and one agent per RunConfig.agents (uid 60001+i, conn c-(i+1), socketpairs, clean env, non-dumpable). Tick barrier: control phase -> TickFrame -> one Submit/Noop per agent until deadline (miss = no-op + anomaly) -> execute in agent_id order -> dispatch/monitor -> flush -> witness ack. Gateway sole assigner of seq (1.., no gaps), record_id_for(seq), ts_us = start+tick*tick_us+slot, conn_id. Determinism: tick clock only, per-consumer RNG streams, HKDF keys from a repro secret in tests (fresh in live). Tests T1 (same seed byte-identical), T2 (faulty == S* before t0), T3-T5. Key-isolation claim stated verbatim. Change requests (CON-02): C2 WitnessCheckpoint.count, C6 RunConfig.fault_tick, C4 empty evidence for barrier.deadline; contracts README key-isolation wording to align.
review:
[panel · changes] PANEL review of ADR-00 (19 Nov). Verdict: CHANGES. All four acceptance criteria are met (899 words, all five sections, barrier and test names present, key-isolation wording verbatim). The design is right: the gateway is the scheduler, it alone assigns seq/ts/id, and wall clock goes only to timing.jsonl. Seeded bench runs with scripted decisions and no rogue will reproduce. Live demo runs and rogue runs will not reproduce as written, and the stall claim has gaps at the I/O level.

MUST-FIX
M1 Human decisions land at a wall-clock tick. The tick at which an approval/suspend/release/revoke lands depends on how fast the human clicks. That tick moves post_alert_tainted, irreversible_released, R and C, so a live demo run cannot be re-run. Ticks are also not paced: an N-tick run can end, and its keys die, before anyone approves the plan. Fix: decision points block the barrier. When a plan or anomaly awaits a human, the gateway does not open tick plan_tick+L (L = RunConfig.decision_latency_ticks) until the decision arrives. A click that arrives early is held until that tick. Bench scripts the same L. A re-run replays the ks.console/ks.recovery Controls from record.jsonl at their recorded ticks. Live clicks then stop breaking determinism, and the Consequences line should change to say so.
M2 S*/t0 disagree across ADRs, so T2 fails by construction. ADR-00 says S* = a clean run with the same seed. ADR-06 says S* = the culprit slot emits no-ops for the WHOLE run. Under ADR-06's definition, crm's legitimate pre-t0 writes are missing from S*, so "faulty == S* before t0" fails and B is polluted. Pick one: culprit no-ops for tick >= fault_tick. t0 is defined three ways: RunConfig.fault_tick (ADR-00), first injected effect (ADR-06), and t0_seq (ADR-05, an estimate). Rename ADR-05's to t0_seq_est. Mark fault_tick like culprit: scorer-only, never read by ks.monitor/ks.recovery. Test: blank fault_tick in config and the record stays identical.
M3 Late and extra frames make records nondeterministic. Collect closes as soon as every agent has answered, so whether a flooder's 2nd/3rd frame lands in tick n or n+1 depends on timing, which shifts seq/ts_us/hash for everyone. Fix: per connection, read exactly ONE frame per tick in FIFO order. A frame tagged <n is recorded as deny/late_frame (not 'expired', which ADR-01/03 use for expiry_tick) and the slot is a no-op. Define future-tick frames (deny). Record them at a fixed position (that agent's slot in the execute phase). A flooder then fills its own socket buffer and only delays itself. Add T3b: a rogue that floods and pre-sends frames still gives T1-identical records.
M4 The barrier is safe but the I/O is not. (a) If a rogue stops reading, its socket buffer fills and a blocking gateway send of TickFrame/ReplyFrame/SignReply stalls the whole barrier. All agent-facing sockets must be non-blocking, with a bounded outbound queue and EOF on overflow. (b) The reader must be non-blocking, bounded by MAX_FRAME_BYTES, and must never wait for an LF (slowloris). (c) Set a per-tick SignRequest quota on the in-gateway signer (ADR-01 mentions rate limits but gives no number). (d) Witness: 'tick n+1 waits for the ack' and 'no ack raises witness_stall' conflict. Say: wait up to the deadline, then proceed and raise witness_stall. Otherwise a hung witness hangs the run, and ADR-02's W-tick detector can never fire.
M5 Stall cost and teardown. (a) A sleep-forever rogue costs 2 s per tick, so 100 ticks take 200 s and the 5-minute demo is gone. Add deterministic eviction: after K consecutive misses, close the connection (EOF, no epoch bump, not a suspend, plus an anomaly). Or state the cost and use a short --tick-deadline-ms on the demo machine. T4 should assert a wall-time bound. (b) Forked children survive the SIGKILL of the agent, keep the reused uid 60001+i, and can break the next run: RLIMIT_NPROC on spawn, CPU contention. Kill by uid or cgroup at teardown, and refuse to start if any process with uid 60000..6000N exists. (c) Set oom_score_adj -1000 on gateway/witness and +1000 on agents, so a memory bomb kills the rogue and not the TCB. (d) Run the --rogue slot at nice 19 / SCHED_IDLE with RLIMIT_CPU, so CPU spin cannot make honest agents miss deadlines. T4 should add CPU-spin and memory-bomb variants and assert 0 honest misses.
M6 Fresh-key projection. Maya's gap is acceptable as stated, because a signature we can reproduce is a signature an attacker can forge. Conditions: (a) the projection is a function in ks.contracts, not an ad-hoc jq, and it must also strip keys.json, which ADR-00 omits although keys.json is in DETERMINISTIC_FILES. (b) T1b must assert that the key-independent artefacts are byte-identical WITHOUT stripping: config, alerts, plans/**, sidestore/**, effects.jsonl, oracle/**, score.json. By contract they do not depend on keys: envelope_hash excludes sig, and idempotency_key is derived from (agent, action, sink, n). (c) DETERMINISTIC_FILES lacks effects.jsonl, oracle/ and score.json, which are exactly the scorer's inputs. Add them through CON-02 or name them in T1. (d) Add RunConfig.key_mode = fresh|repro, so the run dir alone shows that a run is 'not a security run'. (e) In fresh mode the witness generates its own key and the gateway never holds it. Otherwise THREAT-MODEL B3's 'own key' is false and ADR-02 contradicts ADR-00. (f) The repro secret file is 0600 uid 0. --repro-secret is forbidden for D11 live attacks, because a key root on disk voids C1/C4.
M7 The topology omits the operator channel. ks contain / ks recover --apply / ks console --live need to reach the live gateway, and ADR-00 has only path-less agent socketpairs. Specify a socket in a 0700 uid-0 dir with an SO_PEERCRED uid==0 check. Otherwise a rogue uid could forge ks.console Controls, which breaks the THREAT-MODEL target '0 forged Control actions'.

SHOULD-FIX
S1 Use one RNG derivation with ADR-06 (ADR-00 uses sha256(seed||name) streams, ADR-06 uses sha256(seed|agent|tick)). Encode it canonically and length-safe: sha256(canonical([seed,name,tick])). Per-tick derivation means a dropped or late step shifts no later draws.
S2 Make the ts_us slot bound computable. Cap per tick the control-phase records (including recovery steps, with deterministic carry-over), dispatch records and capped late frames, and check that tick_us is larger than the sum.
S3 State in-tick visibility: execution is sequential, so payments sees crm's same-tick write, which matches ADR-05(c). ADR-06's 'reader sees writes from earlier ticks' is wrong for adapter reads.
S4 T4 'other agents' records unchanged' must mean a per-agent projection (tick, tool, args_hash, decision, read/write sets), because seq/ts/hash shift. T1 should run the gateway under different PYTHONHASHSEEDs. Rogue byte-identity (ADR-07 test 6) holds only for rogue code that draws only from its stream seed.
S5 C4: the barrier.deadline anomaly cannot name its connection, because Alert.conn_id is signature-only (validator) and ADR-04 says detectors never name anyone. Add a conn_id allowance to the CON-02 request, and ADR-04 adds barrier.deadline (never hard) to its catalogue.
S6 A post-run 'ks recover --dry-run' writes into plans/ of an evidence dir that T1 compares. Write it outside the run dir.
Word budget: the fixes will not fit in 900 words. Trim lifecycle steps 1-2 (already in ADR-02/contracts) and push details into test names.

DEMO, fresh keys: never say 'byte-identical' for a live run. Beat: run F2+ twice with fresh keys; ks verify OK on both, each under its own keys; sha256(score.json) is identical; 'ks repro A B' (ADR-07 to add) reports 0 differences outside {sig, hash, prev_hash, gw_sig, head, pub}. Line: 'Reproducible behaviour, unrepeatable signatures: a signature we could reproduce, an attacker could forge.' Byte-identical claims are reserved for the >=20-seed bench under --repro-secret, labelled 'not a security run'. Never publish the secret of a run presented as evidence.
